v: The words of Amos,[^1] who was one of the sheep breeders[^2] of Tekoa,[^3] which he saw[^4] concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.[^5]

דִּבְרֵ֣י עָמ֔וֹס אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה בַנֹּקְדִ֖ים מִתְּק֑וֹעַ אֲשֶׁר֩ חָזָ֨ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בִּימֵ֣י ׀ עֻזִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֗ה וּבִימֵ֞י יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן־יוֹאָשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁנָתַ֖יִם לִפְנֵ֥י הָרָֽעַשׁ׃
He said: The LORD[^6] roars from Zion and raises his voice[^7] from Jerusalem. The pastures of the shepherds mourn,[^8] and the top of Carmel[^9] withers.
וַיֹּאמַ֓ר ׀ יְהוָה֙ מִצִיּ֣וֹן יִשְׁאָ֔ג וּמִירוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם יִתֵּ֣ן קוֹל֑וֹ וְאָֽבְלוּ֙ נְא֣וֹת הָרֹעִ֔ים וְיָבֵ֖שׁ רֹ֥אשׁ הַכַּרְמֶֽל׃ פ
This is what the LORD says:[^10] For three crimes[^11] of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back,[^12] because they threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron.[^13]
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵ֣י דַמֶּ֔שֶׂק וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַל־דּוּשָׁ֛ם בַּחֲרֻצ֥וֹת הַבַּרְזֶ֖ל אֶת־הַגִּלְעָֽד׃
So I will send fire on the house of Hazael, and it will devour the fortresses[^14] of Ben-hadad.[^15]
וְשִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּבֵ֣ית חֲזָאֵ֑ל וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנ֥וֹת בֶּן־הֲדָֽד׃

I will break the gate bar of Damascus. I will cut off the one who sits enthroned[^16] in the Valley of Aven, and the one who holds the scepter in Beth-eden.[^17] The people of Aram will go into exile to Kir,[^18] says the LORD.
וְשָֽׁבַרְתִּי֙ בְּרִ֣יחַ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י יוֹשֵׁב֙ מִבִּקְעַת־אָ֔וֶן וְתוֹמֵ֥ךְ שֵׁ֖בֶט מִבֵּ֣ית עֶ֑דֶן וְגָל֧וּ עַם־אֲרָ֛ם קִ֖ירָה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ פ
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried away whole communities[^19] into exile, to hand them over to Edom.
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵ֣י עַזָּ֔ה וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַל־הַגְלוֹתָ֛ם גָּל֥וּת שְׁלֵמָ֖ה לְהַסְגִּ֥יר לֶאֱדֽוֹם׃
So I will send fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its fortresses.
וְשִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּחוֹמַ֣ת עַזָּ֑ה וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃

I will cut off the one who sits enthroned in Ashdod, and the one who holds the scepter in Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish,[^20] says the Lord GOD.[^21]
וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י יוֹשֵׁב֙ מֵֽאַשְׁדּ֔וֹד וְתוֹמֵ֥ךְ שֵׁ֖בֶט מֵֽאַשְׁקְל֑וֹן וַהֲשִׁיב֨וֹתִי יָדִ֜י עַל־עֶקְר֗וֹן וְאָֽבְדוּ֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ פ
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they handed over whole communities to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brothers.[^22]
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵי־צֹ֔ר וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַֽל־הַסְגִּירָ֞ם גָּל֤וּת שְׁלֵמָה֙ לֶאֱד֔וֹם וְלֹ֥א זָכְר֖וּ בְּרִ֥ית אַחִֽים׃
So I will send fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its fortresses.
וְשִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּח֣וֹמַת צֹ֑ר וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃ פ

This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother[^23] with the sword and stifled all pity.[^24] His anger tore without end, and he kept his fury forever.[^25]
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵ֣י אֱד֔וֹם וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַל־רָדְפ֨וֹ בַחֶ֤רֶב אָחִיו֙ וְשִׁחֵ֣ת רַחֲמָ֔יו וַיִּטְרֹ֤ף לָעַד֙ אַפּ֔וֹ וְעֶבְרָת֖וֹ שְׁמָ֥רָה נֶֽצַח׃
So I will send fire on Teman, and it will devour the fortresses of Bozrah.[^26]
וְשִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי אֵ֖שׁ בְּתֵימָ֑ן וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנ֥וֹת בָּצְרָֽה׃ פ
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of the Ammonites, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge their territory.
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֔וֹן וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַל־בִּקְעָם֙ הָר֣וֹת הַגִּלְעָ֔ד לְמַ֖עַן הַרְחִ֥יב אֶת־גְּבוּלָֽם׃
So I will kindle a fire on the wall of Rabbah,[^27] and it will devour its fortresses, with a battle cry on the day of battle, with a storm on the day of the whirlwind.
וְהִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּחוֹמַ֣ת רַבָּ֔ה וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ בִּתְרוּעָה֙ בְּי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֔ה בְּסַ֖עַר בְּי֥וֹם סוּפָֽה
Their king[^28] will go into exile, he and his officials together, says the LORD.
וְהָלַ֥ךְ מַלְכָּ֖ם בַּגּוֹלָ֑ה ה֧וּא וְשָׂרָ֛יו יַחְדָּ֖ו אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ פ

n.1: A name from the verb "to carry a load".
n.2: Hebrew *noqedim*, owners or keepers of sheep. The king of Moab is called a *noqed* in 2 Kings 3:4. Amos also calls himself a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs (7:14).
n.3: A town in the hills of Judah, about 10 miles (16 km) south of Jerusalem (2 Samuel 14:2).
n.4: Hebrew *chazah*, "see", used of what a prophet receives in a vision.
n.5: Uzziah reigned in Judah about 792–740 BC, and Jeroboam II in Israel about 793–753 BC. Amos probably spoke about 760 BC. The earthquake was remembered long afterward (Zechariah 14:5).
n.6: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.7: Literally "gives his voice". The same line is found in Joel 4:16 (3:16 in most English Bibles). The LORD roars like a lion (3:4, 8).
n.8: Or "dry up". The Hebrew verb *aval* can mean either.
n.9: The wooded ridge above the coast of northern Israel, one of the most fertile places in the land.
n.10: In Amos's poetry, as in Isaiah, the words of the prophet and the words of the LORD alternate. The LORD's words in the poems are not put in quotation marks.
n.11: Hebrew *pesha*, "rebellion, transgression", a deliberate breaking of what is right. Traditionally "transgressions". *For three … and for four*: a number saying (Proverbs 30:15–31). The crimes are many, and the last fills the measure. Each oracle in 1:3–2:16 then names one or more of them.
n.12: Literally "I will not turn it back", that is, the punishment, or the word the LORD has spoken. Also in verses 6, 9, 11 and 13 and in 2:1, 4 and 6.
n.13: Threshing sledges were heavy boards studded underneath with stones or iron spikes, dragged over grain. Gilead, east of the Jordan, belonged to Israel. Compare 2 Kings 10:32–33; 13:7.
n.14: Hebrew *armenot*, the fortified palaces of a city. Also in verses 7, 10, 12 and 14.
n.15: Hazael and his son Ben-hadad were kings of Aram, whose capital was Damascus (2 Kings 8:7–15; 13:3, 24).
n.17: *Valley of Aven* means "valley of wickedness", perhaps the valley between the Lebanon ranges. *Beth-eden* means "house of delight", probably the Aramean state of Bit-adini on the Euphrates.
n.18: The land the Arameans had come from (9:7). Compare 2 Kings 16:9.
n.19: Literally "a complete exile". Also in verse 9. The people were sold as slaves.
n.20: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron were four of the five chief cities of the Philistines. The fifth, Gath, is not named (compare 6:2).
n.21: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.22: A treaty that bound the two sides as "brothers", perhaps with Israel (1 Kings 5:26, 5:12 in most English Bibles; 9:13).
n.23: Israel. Edom was descended from Esau, the brother of Jacob (Genesis 25:24–26; 36:1).
n.25: Or "his fury kept watch forever". Many scholars read "he kept his anger forever" in the first line too, with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.26: Teman was a region of Edom, and Bozrah one of its chief cities.
n.27: The capital of the Ammonites, modern Amman in Jordan.
n.28: Hebrew *malkam*, "their king". The same consonants can be read *Milkom*, Milcom, the god of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11:5). A similar line in Jeremiah 49:3 adds "his priests".

v: This is what the LORD[^1] says: For three crimes of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back,[^2] because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.[^3]
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַל־שָׂרְפ֛וֹ עַצְמ֥וֹת מֶֽלֶךְ־אֱד֖וֹם לַשִּֽׂיד׃
So I will send fire on Moab, and it will devour the fortresses of Kerioth.[^4] Moab will die amid the uproar, with a battle cry and the sound of the ram's horn.[^5]
וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי־אֵ֣שׁ בְּמוֹאָ֔ב וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנ֣וֹת הַקְּרִיּ֑וֹת וּמֵ֤ת בְּשָׁאוֹן֙ מוֹאָ֔ב בִּתְרוּעָ֖ה בְּק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃
I will cut off the ruler[^6] from within her and kill all her officials with him, says the LORD.
וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י שׁוֹפֵ֖ט מִקִּרְבָּ֑הּ וְכָל־שָׂרֶ֛יהָ אֶהֱר֥וֹג עִמּ֖וֹ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ פ

This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the instruction[^7] of the LORD and did not keep his decrees. Their lies,[^8] which their ancestors followed, have led them astray.

כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַֽל־מָאֳסָ֞ם אֶת־תּוֹרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה וְחֻקָּיו֙ לֹ֣א שָׁמָ֔רוּ וַיַּתְעוּם֙ כִּזְבֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הָלְכ֥וּ אֲבוֹתָ֖ם אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
So I will send fire on Judah, and it will devour the fortresses of Jerusalem.
וְשִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי אֵ֖שׁ בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה וְאָכְלָ֖ה אַרְמְנ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ פ
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sell the innocent[^9] for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals.[^10]
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פִּשְׁעֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ עַל־מִכְרָ֤ם בַּכֶּ֙סֶף֙ צַדִּ֔יק וְאֶבְי֖וֹן בַּעֲב֥וּר נַעֲלָֽיִם׃
They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the ground[^11] and push the humble out of the way.[^12] A man and his father go to the same young woman,[^13] and so they profane my holy name.
הַשֹּׁאֲפִ֤ים עַל־עֲפַר־אֶ֙רֶץ֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ דַּלִּ֔ים וְדֶ֥רֶךְ עֲנָוִ֖ים יַטּ֑וּ וְאִ֣ישׁ וְאָבִ֗יו יֵֽלְכוּ֙ אֶל־הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה לְמַ֥עַן חַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי׃
They stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge,[^14] and in the house of their God[^15] they drink wine taken from those they have fined.
וְעַל־בְּגָדִ֤ים חֲבֻלִים֙ יַטּ֔וּ אֵ֖צֶל כָּל־מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וְיֵ֤ין עֲנוּשִׁים֙ יִשְׁתּ֔וּ בֵּ֖ית אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite[^16] before them, though he was as tall as the cedars and as strong as the oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
וְאָ֨נֹכִ֜י הִשְׁמַ֤דְתִּי אֶת־הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר כְּגֹ֤בַהּ אֲרָזִים֙ גָּבְה֔וֹ וְחָסֹ֥ן ה֖וּא כָּֽאַלּוֹנִ֑ים וָאַשְׁמִ֤יד פִּרְיוֹ֙ מִמַּ֔עַל וְשָׁרָשָׁ֖יו מִתָּֽחַת׃
It was I who brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you forty years in the wilderness, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
וְאָנֹכִ֛י הֶעֱלֵ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וָאוֹלֵ֨ךְ אֶתְכֶ֤ם בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה לָרֶ֖שֶׁת אֶת־אֶ֥רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃
I raised up some of your sons to be prophets, and some of your young men to be Nazirites.[^17] Is it not so, people of Israel? declares the LORD.[^18]
וָאָקִ֤ים מִבְּנֵיכֶם֙ לִנְבִיאִ֔ים וּמִבַּחוּרֵיכֶ֖ם לִנְזִרִ֑ים הַאַ֥ף אֵֽין־זֹ֛את בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and you commanded the prophets, "Do not prophesy."
וַתַּשְׁק֥וּ אֶת־הַנְּזִרִ֖ים יָ֑יִן וְעַל־הַנְּבִיאִים֙ צִוִּיתֶ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֖א תִּנָּבְאֽוּ׃
Look, I am going to crush you down where you stand,[^19] as a cart crushes when it is full of sheaves.
הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י מֵעִ֖יק תַּחְתֵּיכֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר תָּעִיק֙ הָעֲגָלָ֔ה הַֽמְלֵאָ֥ה לָ֖הּ עָמִֽיר׃
The swift will have nowhere to flee;[^20] the strong will not hold on to his strength, and the warrior will not save his life.
וְאָבַ֤ד מָנוֹס֙ מִקָּ֔ל וְחָזָ֖ק לֹא־יְאַמֵּ֣ץ כֹּח֑וֹ וְגִבּ֖וֹר לֹא־יְמַלֵּ֥ט נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
The one who handles the bow will not stand his ground, the swift of foot will not escape, and the one who rides the horse will not save his life.
וְתֹפֵ֤שׂ הַקֶּ֙שֶׁת֙ לֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֔ד וְקַ֥ל בְּרַגְלָ֖יו לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּ֑ט וְרֹכֵ֣ב הַסּ֔וּס לֹ֥א יְמַלֵּ֖ט נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
Even the bravest of the warriors[^21] will flee naked on that day, declares the LORD.
וְאַמִּ֥יץ לִבּ֖וֹ בַּגִּבּוֹרִ֑ים עָר֛וֹם יָנ֥וּס בַּיּוֹם־הַה֖וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Burning the bones of the dead was an outrage against them (compare 2 Kings 23:16).
n.4: A city of Moab (Jeremiah 48:24). Or "the fortresses of its cities".
n.5: Hebrew *shofar*, a trumpet made from a ram's horn, sounded as an alarm in war.
n.6: Hebrew *shofet*, "judge", here the one who governs.
n.9: Hebrew *tsaddiq*, "righteous", here one who is in the right, perhaps in a lawsuit.
n.10: Perhaps for a debt as small as the price of sandals, or for a bribe. Compare 8:6.
n.11: Literally "who pant for the dust of the earth on the head of the poor". The verb *sha'af* means "pant, long for", but here it may be a form of *shuf*, "trample". If it means "long for", they covet even the dust that the poor throw on their heads in grief.
n.12: Literally "turn aside the way of the humble", that is, deny them justice.
n.13: Hebrew *na'arah*, a girl or young woman, perhaps a servant in the household. Compare Leviticus 18:8, 15.
n.14: The law required a cloak taken as a pledge for a debt to be given back before night (Exodus 22:25–26, 22:26–27 in most English Bibles; Deuteronomy 24:12–13).
n.16: Here the peoples who lived in Canaan before Israel (Genesis 15:16; Numbers 13:32–33).
n.17: People dedicated to God by a vow, who drank no wine (Numbers 6:1–21).
n.18: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verse 16.
n.19: Literally "I am pressing beneath you". The Hebrew verb *'uq* is found only here, and its meaning is uncertain: perhaps "press down", or "split open", as the ground splits under a heavy cart.
n.20: Literally "flight will perish from the swift".
n.21: Literally "the stout of heart among the warriors".

v: Hear this word that the LORD[^1] has spoken against you, people of Israel, against the whole clan that I brought up from the land of Egypt:
שִׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַ֚ל כָּל־הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֶעֱלֵ֛יתִי מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃
You alone have I known[^2] of all the clans of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all your wrongdoing.
רַ֚ק אֶתְכֶ֣ם יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִכֹּ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת הָאֲדָמָ֑ה עַל־כֵּן֙ אֶפְקֹ֣ד עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת כָּל־עֲוֺנֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃
Do two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
הֲיֵלְכ֥וּ שְׁנַ֖יִם יַחְדָּ֑ו בִּלְתִּ֖י אִם־נוֹעָֽדוּ׃
Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion growl from its den unless it has caught something?
הֲיִשְׁאַ֤ג אַרְיֵה֙ בַּיַּ֔עַר וְטֶ֖רֶף אֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ הֲיִתֵּ֨ן כְּפִ֤יר קוֹלוֹ֙ מִמְּעֹ֣נָת֔וֹ בִּלְתִּ֖י אִם־לָכָֽד׃
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when no snare[^3] is set for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground when it has caught nothing?
הֲתִפֹּ֤ל צִפּוֹר֙ עַל־פַּ֣ח הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמוֹקֵ֖שׁ אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ הֲיַֽעֲלֶה־פַּח֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וְלָכ֖וֹד לֹ֥א יִלְכּֽוֹד׃
If a ram's horn[^4] is blown in a city, are the people not afraid? If disaster comes to a city, has the LORD not done it?
אִם־יִתָּקַ֤ע שׁוֹפָר֙ בְּעִ֔יר וְעָ֖ם לֹ֣א יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ אִם־תִּהְיֶ֤ה רָעָה֙ בְּעִ֔יר וַיהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א עָשָֽׂה׃
Surely the Lord GOD[^5] does nothing without revealing his plan[^6] to his servants the prophets.
כִּ֣י לֹ֧א יַעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר כִּ֚י אִם־גָּלָ֣ה סוֹד֔וֹ אֶל־עֲבָדָ֖יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃
The lion has roared; who will not be afraid? The Lord GOD has spoken; who can do anything but prophesy?
אַרְיֵ֥ה שָׁאָ֖ג מִ֣י לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ דִּבֶּ֔ר מִ֖י לֹ֥א יִנָּבֵֽא׃

Proclaim it to the fortresses in Ashdod[^7] and to the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: "Gather on the mountains of Samaria, and see the great turmoil within her and the oppression in her midst."
הַשְׁמִ֙יעוּ֙ עַל־אַרְמְנ֣וֹת בְּאַשְׁדּ֔וֹד וְעַֽל־אַרְמְנ֖וֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאִמְר֗וּ הֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ עַל־הָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וּרְא֞וּ מְהוּמֹ֤ת רַבּוֹת֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ וַעֲשׁוּקִ֖ים בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃
They do not know how to do what is right, declares the LORD,[^8] those who store up violence and destruction in their fortresses.
וְלֹֽא־יָדְע֥וּ עֲשׂוֹת־נְכֹחָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה הָאֽ[m]וֹצְרִ֛ים חָמָ֥ס וָשֹׁ֖ד בְּאַרְמְנֽוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃ פ
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: An enemy will surround the land.[^9] He will strip you of your strength,[^10] and your fortresses will be plundered.
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה צַ֖ר וּסְבִ֣יב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהוֹרִ֤ד מִמֵּךְ֙ עֻזֵּ֔ךְ וְנָבֹ֖זּוּ אַרְמְנוֹתָֽיִךְ׃

This is what the LORD says: As a shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth two legs or a piece of an ear,[^11] so the people of Israel who live in Samaria will be rescued, with the corner of a couch and a piece of a bed.[^12]

כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַצִּ֨יל הָרֹעֶ֜ה מִפִּ֧י הָאֲרִ֛י שְׁתֵּ֥י כְרָעַ֖יִם א֣וֹ בְדַל־אֹ֑זֶן כֵּ֣ן יִנָּצְל֞וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּפְאַ֥ת מִטָּ֖ה וּבִדְמֶ֥שֶׁק עָֽרֶשׂ׃
Hear, and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of Armies.[^13]
שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהָעִ֖ידוּ בְּבֵ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַצְּבָאֽוֹת׃
On the day I punish Israel for its crimes,[^14] I will punish the altars of Bethel.[^15] The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם פָּקְדִ֥י פִשְׁעֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עָלָ֑יו וּפָֽקַדְתִּי֙ עַל־מִזְבְּח֣וֹת בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וְנִגְדְּעוּ֙ קַרְנ֣וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְנָפְל֖וּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃
I will strike the winter house together with the summer house. The houses of ivory[^16] will perish, and the great houses[^17] will come to an end, declares the LORD.
וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י בֵית־הַחֹ֖רֶף עַל־בֵּ֣ית הַקָּ֑יִץ וְאָבְד֞וּ בָּתֵּ֣י הַשֵּׁ֗ן וְסָפ֛וּ בָּתִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: That is, chosen and cared for as my own (Genesis 18:19; Hosea 13:5).
n.3: Hebrew *moqesh*, perhaps the bait or the trigger of the trap.
n.4: Hebrew *shofar*, a trumpet made from a ram's horn, sounded as an alarm in war.
n.5: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. Also in verses 8, 11 and 13.
n.6: Hebrew *sod*, the private counsel of a ruler and his advisers (Jeremiah 23:18, 22).
n.8: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 13 and 15.
n.9: Literally "An enemy, and around the land!" The Hebrew is abrupt.
n.10: Literally "He will bring down your strength from you". The Hebrew addresses Samaria as "you" (feminine).
n.11: A shepherd brought back such remains as proof that a wild animal had killed the sheep, so that he would not have to repay it (Exodus 22:12, 22:13 in most English Bibles; Genesis 31:39).
n.12: The meaning is uncertain. Literally "with the corner of a bed and with Damascus of a couch". *Damascus* may be a word for fine fabric, or a word for part of a couch. Or "so the people of Israel will be rescued, those who sit in Samaria on the corner of a bed and on the cushions of a couch".
n.13: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH Elohei ha-tseva'ot*, "the Lord GOD, the God of the Armies". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Compare "the LORD of Armies", traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty".
n.14: Literally "On the day I punish the crimes of Israel on him".
n.15: The royal shrine of the northern kingdom (7:13; 1 Kings 12:28–33). The horns were the projections at the four corners of an altar. A person seeking refuge took hold of them (1 Kings 1:50).
n.16: Houses decorated with carved ivory panels, like Ahab's palace in Samaria (1 Kings 22:39).

v: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan[^1] on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to your husbands,[^2] "Bring us something to drink!"
שִׁמְע֞וּ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה פָּר֤וֹת הַבָּשָׁן֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּהַ֣ר שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן הָעֹשְׁק֣וֹת דַּלִּ֔ים הָרֹצְצ֖וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים הָאֹמְרֹ֥ת לַאֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֖ם הָבִ֥יאָה וְנִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
The Lord GOD[^3] has sworn by his holiness: Look, the days are coming on you when you will be carried away with hooks, and the last of you with fishhooks.[^4]
נִשְׁבַּ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ בְּקָדְשׁ֔וֹ כִּ֛י הִנֵּ֥ה יָמִ֖ים בָּאִ֣ים עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְנִשָּׂ֤א אֶתְכֶם֙ בְּצִנּ֔וֹת וְאַחֲרִיתְכֶ֖ן בְּסִיר֥וֹת דּוּגָֽה׃
You will go out through the breaches in the wall, each woman straight ahead, and you will be thrown out toward Harmon,[^5] declares the LORD.[^6]
וּפְרָצִ֥ים תֵּצֶ֖אנָה אִשָּׁ֣ה נֶגְדָּ֑הּ וְהִשְׁלַכְתֶּ֥נָה הַהַרְמ֖וֹנָה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Come to Bethel and rebel;[^7] go to Gilgal[^8] and rebel all the more! Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every third day.[^9]
בֹּ֤אוּ בֵֽית־אֵל֙ וּפִשְׁע֔וּ הַגִּלְגָּ֖ל הַרְבּ֣וּ לִפְשֹׁ֑עַ וְהָבִ֤יאוּ לַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ זִבְחֵיכֶ֔ם לִשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים מַעְשְׂרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃
Burn a thanksgiving offering of bread made with yeast,[^10] and proclaim your freewill offerings; announce them! For that is what you love to do, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
וְקַטֵּ֤ר מֵֽחָמֵץ֙ תּוֹדָ֔ה וְקִרְא֥וּ נְדָב֖וֹת הַשְׁמִ֑יעוּ כִּ֣י כֵ֤ן אֲהַבְתֶּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
I gave you clean teeth[^11] in all your cities and a lack of bread in all your places, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
וְגַם־אֲנִי֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם נִקְי֤וֹן שִׁנַּ֙יִם֙ בְּכָל־עָ֣רֵיכֶ֔ם וְחֹ֣סֶר לֶ֔חֶם בְּכֹ֖ל מְקוֹמֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

I also held back the rain from you when there were still three months to the harvest.[^12] I sent rain on one city and sent no rain on another city. One field had rain, and the field that had no rain dried up.

וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִי֩ מָנַ֨עְתִּי מִכֶּ֜ם אֶת־הַגֶּ֗שֶׁם בְּע֨וֹד שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ לַקָּצִ֔יר וְהִמְטַרְתִּי֙ עַל־עִ֣יר אֶחָ֔ת וְעַל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֖ת לֹ֣א אַמְטִ֑יר חֶלְקָ֤ה אַחַת֙ תִּמָּטֵ֔ר וְחֶלְקָ֛ה אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹֽא־תַמְטִ֥יר עָלֶ֖יהָ תִּיבָֽשׁ׃
Two or three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and could not drink their fill, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
וְנָע֡וּ שְׁתַּיִם֩ שָׁלֹ֨שׁ עָרִ֜ים אֶל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֛ת לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֑עוּ וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
I struck you with blight and mildew.[^13] Your many gardens and vineyards,[^14] your fig trees and your olive trees, the cutting locust[^15] devoured, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
הִכֵּ֣יתִי אֶתְכֶם֮ בַּשִּׁדָּפ֣וֹן וּבַיֵּרָקוֹן֒ הַרְבּ֨וֹת גַּנּוֹתֵיכֶ֧ם וְכַרְמֵיכֶ֛ם וּתְאֵנֵיכֶ֥ם וְזֵיתֵיכֶ֖ם יֹאכַ֣ל הַגָּזָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס

I sent a plague among you as I did in Egypt.[^16] I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses were captured.[^17] I made the stench of your camps rise into your nostrils, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.

שִׁלַּ֨חְתִּי בָכֶ֥ם דֶּ֙בֶר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם הָרַ֤גְתִּי בַחֶ֙רֶב֙ בַּח֣וּרֵיכֶ֔ם עִ֖ם שְׁבִ֣י סֽוּסֵיכֶ֑ם וָאַעֲלֶ֞ה בְּאֹ֤שׁ מַחֲנֵיכֶם֙ וּֽבְאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
I overthrew some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah,[^18] and you were like a burning stick snatched from the fire, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
הָפַ֣כְתִּי בָכֶ֗ם כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֤ת אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־סְדֹ֣ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֔ה וַתִּהְי֕וּ כְּא֖וּד מֻצָּ֣ל מִשְׂרֵפָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you,[^19] prepare to meet your God, Israel!
לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֵ֚קֶב כִּֽי־זֹ֣את אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ הִכּ֥וֹן לִקְרַאת־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

For look, he who forms the mountains and creates the wind,[^20] who tells human beings what his thoughts are,[^21] who turns the dawn into darkness,[^22] and treads on the heights of the earth: the LORD, the God of Armies,[^23] is his name.
כִּ֡י הִנֵּה֩ יוֹצֵ֨ר הָרִ֜ים וּבֹרֵ֣א ר֗וּחַ וּמַגִּ֤יד לְאָדָם֙ מַה־שֵּׂח֔וֹ עֹשֵׂ֥ה שַׁ֙חַר֙ עֵיפָ֔ה וְדֹרֵ֖ךְ עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי אָ֑רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ ס

n.1: A fertile highland east of the Sea of Galilee, famous for its well-fed cattle (Deuteronomy 32:14; Psalm 22:13, 22:12 in most English Bibles). Here the phrase describes the wealthy women of Samaria.
n.3: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The Lord GOD* is also in verse 5.
n.4: The meaning of both words for hooks is uncertain. Or "in baskets … in fishing pots". *The last of you* may also mean "your descendants".
n.5: The place is unknown. Perhaps Mount Hermon, in the north, is meant. The verb is active, literally "you will throw", perhaps "you will throw yourselves".
n.6: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 5–11.
n.7: The verb is related to *pesha*, "crime, rebellion" (1:3). The invitation is ironic: their worship at the shrines is itself rebellion.
n.8: An ancient shrine near Jericho (Joshua 4:19–20; 1 Samuel 11:14–15; Hosea 4:15). Bethel, also a shrine, is about 11 miles (18 km) north of Jerusalem.
n.9: Literally "for three days". Or "on the third day", perhaps of a pilgrimage. The law required tithes once a year, and a special tithe every third year (Deuteronomy 14:22–29).
n.10: Bread made with yeast was eaten with a thanksgiving offering, but no yeast was to be burned on the altar (Leviticus 2:11; 7:13).
n.12: The late rains of winter and early spring, which the grain needed before the harvest.
n.13: Blight, scorching by the hot east wind, and mildew, a disease that turns grain yellow, are named together in Deuteronomy 28:22 and 1 Kings 8:37.
n.14: Literally "the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards". Some scholars read "I laid waste your gardens and your vineyards", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.15: Hebrew *gazam*, one of the four words for locusts in Joel 1:4. They may be different kinds of locust or stages in the insect's growth.
n.16: Literally "in the way of Egypt", that is, like the plagues of Egypt (Exodus 9:3; Deuteronomy 28:27, 60). Or "on the road to Egypt".
n.17: Literally "with the captivity of your horses".
n.18: Genesis 19:24–25. The verb *overthrew* is the word used of their destruction.
n.19: What the LORD will do is not stated.
n.20: Or "spirit". Hebrew *ruach* can mean wind, breath or spirit.
n.21: Or "their thoughts": the Hebrew may mean God's thoughts or human thoughts. The meaning of the word, *seach*, found only here, is uncertain.
n.22: Or "who makes the dawn and the darkness". This verse is the first of three hymns in Amos that praise the LORD as Creator and end with his name (5:8–9; 9:5–6).
n.23: Hebrew *YHWH Elohei tseva'ot*, "the LORD, the God of Armies". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Compare "the LORD of Armies", traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty".

v: Hear this word, which I take up over you as a lament,[^1] house of Israel:
שִׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֜י נֹשֵׂ֧א עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם קִינָ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Fallen, never to rise again, is the virgin Israel.[^2] She lies abandoned on her land, with no one to raise her up.
נָֽפְלָה֙ לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֣יף ק֔וּם בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נִטְּשָׁ֥ה עַל־אַדְמָתָ֖הּ אֵ֥ין מְקִימָֽהּ׃

For this is what the Lord GOD[^3] says: The city that marches out a thousand strong will have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred strong will have ten left, for the house of Israel.
כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הָעִ֛יר הַיֹּצֵ֥את אֶ֖לֶף תַּשְׁאִ֣יר מֵאָ֑ה וְהַיּוֹצֵ֥את מֵאָ֛ה תַּשְׁאִ֥יר עֲשָׂרָ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס
For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: Seek me and live!
כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דִּרְשׁ֖וּנִי וִֽחְיֽוּ׃
But do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba.[^4] For Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.[^5]
וְאַֽל־תִּדְרְשׁוּ֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וְהַגִּלְגָּל֙ לֹ֣א תָבֹ֔אוּ וּבְאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע לֹ֣א תַעֲבֹ֑רוּ כִּ֤י הַגִּלְגָּל֙ גָּלֹ֣ה יִגְלֶ֔ה וּבֵֽית־אֵ֖ל יִהְיֶ֥ה לְאָֽוֶן׃
Seek the LORD and live, or he will break out like fire on the house of Joseph,[^6] and it will devour, with no one to put it out for Bethel.
דִּרְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וִֽחְי֑וּ פֶּן־יִצְלַ֤ח כָּאֵשׁ֙ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף וְאָכְלָ֥ה וְאֵין־מְכַבֶּ֖ה לְבֵֽית־אֵֽל׃
You who turn justice into wormwood[^7] and throw righteousness to the ground!
הַהֹפְכִ֥ים לְלַעֲנָ֖ה מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה לָאָ֥רֶץ הִנִּֽיחוּ׃

He who made the Pleiades and Orion,[^8] who turns deep darkness[^9] into morning and darkens day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth: the LORD is his name.
עֹשֵׂ֨ה כִימָ֜ה וּכְסִ֗יל וְהֹפֵ֤ךְ לַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ צַלְמָ֔וֶת וְי֖וֹם לַ֣יְלָה הֶחְשִׁ֑יךְ הַקּוֹרֵ֣א לְמֵֽי־הַיָּ֗ם וַֽיִּשְׁפְּכֵ֛ם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃ ס
He makes destruction flash out[^10] against the strong, and destruction comes on the fortress.
הַמַּבְלִ֥יג שֹׁ֖ד עַל־עָ֑ז וְשֹׁ֖ד עַל־מִבְצָ֥ר יָבֽוֹא׃
They hate the one who gives correction in the gate,[^11] and they detest the one who speaks with integrity.
שָׂנְא֥וּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מוֹכִ֑יחַ וְדֹבֵ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יְתָעֵֽבוּ׃

Therefore, because you trample on the poor[^12] and take from them a levy of grain, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.[^13]
לָ֠כֵן יַ֣עַן בּוֹשַׁסְכֶ֞ם עַל־דָּ֗ל וּמַשְׂאַת־בַּר֙ תִּקְח֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ בָּתֵּ֥י גָזִ֛ית בְּנִיתֶ֖ם וְלֹא־תֵ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֑ם כַּרְמֵי־חֶ֣מֶד נְטַעְתֶּ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁתּ֖וּ אֶת־יֵינָֽם׃
For I know how many your crimes are and how great your sins: you who harass the innocent, who take bribes,[^14] and who turn aside the needy in the gate.
כִּ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ רַבִּ֣ים פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים חַטֹּֽאתֵיכֶ֑ם צֹרְרֵ֤י צַדִּיק֙ לֹ֣קְחֵי כֹ֔פֶר וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים בַּשַּׁ֥עַר הִטּֽוּ׃
Therefore the prudent will keep silent at such a time, for it is an evil time.
לָכֵ֗ן הַמַּשְׂכִּ֛יל בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖יא יִדֹּ֑ם כִּ֛י עֵ֥ת רָעָ֖ה הִֽיא׃
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live. Then the LORD, the God of Armies,[^15] will be with you, as you say he is.
דִּרְשׁוּ־ט֥וֹב וְאַל־רָ֖ע לְמַ֣עַן תִּֽחְי֑וּ וִיהִי־כֵ֞ן יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֛וֹת אִתְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּֽם׃
Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, the God of Armies, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.
שִׂנְאוּ־רָע֙ וְאֶ֣הֱבוּ ט֔וֹב וְהַצִּ֥יגוּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט אוּלַ֗י יֽ͏ֶחֱנַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יוֹסֵֽף׃ ס

Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Armies, the Lord,[^16] says: There will be wailing in all the squares, and in all the streets they will say, "Alas! Alas!"[^17] They will call the farmer to mourning, and those skilled in lament[^18] to wailing.
לָ֠כֵן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ אֲדֹנָ֔י בְּכָל־רְחֹב֣וֹת מִסְפֵּ֔ד וּבְכָל־חוּצ֖וֹת יֹאמְר֣וּ הוֹ־ה֑וֹ וְקָרְא֤וּ אִכָּר֙ אֶל־אֵ֔בֶל וּמִסְפֵּ֖ד אֶל־י֥וֹדְעֵי נֶֽהִי׃
In all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst,[^19] says the LORD.
וּבְכָל־כְּרָמִ֖ים מִסְפֵּ֑ד כִּֽי־אֶעֱבֹ֥ר בְּקִרְבְּךָ֖ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Woe to[^20] you who long for the day of the LORD![^21] Why would you want the day of the LORD? It is darkness, and not light.
ה֥וֹי הַמִּתְאַוִּ֖ים אֶת־י֣וֹם יְהוָ֑ה לָמָּה־זֶּ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם י֥וֹם יְהוָ֖ה הוּא־חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־אֽוֹר׃
It will be as when someone flees from a lion and a bear meets him, or goes into the house and leans his hand against the wall, and a snake bites him.
כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנ֥וּס אִישׁ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָאֲרִ֔י וּפְגָע֖וֹ הַדֹּ֑ב וּבָ֣א הַבַּ֔יִת וְסָמַ֤ךְ יָדוֹ֙ עַל־הַקִּ֔יר וּנְשָׁכ֖וֹ הַנָּחָֽשׁ׃
Is not the day of the LORD darkness, and not light, gloom with no brightness in it?
הֲלֹא־חֹ֛שֶׁךְ י֥וֹם יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹא־א֑וֹר וְאָפֵ֖ל וְלֹא־נֹ֥גַֽהּ לֽוֹ׃
I hate, I reject your festivals; I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.[^22]
שָׂנֵ֥אתִי מָאַ֖סְתִּי חַגֵּיכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֥א אָרִ֖יחַ בְּעַצְּרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃
Even though you offer me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them; I will not look at the fellowship offerings[^23] of your fattened animals.
כִּ֣י אִם־תַּעֲלוּ־לִ֥י עֹל֛וֹת וּמִנְחֹתֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֣א אֶרְצֶ֑ה וְשֶׁ֥לֶם מְרִיאֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א אַבִּֽיט׃
Take away from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps.
הָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלַ֖י הֲמ֣וֹן שִׁרֶ֑יךָ וְזִמְרַ֥ת נְבָלֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
But let justice roll on like waters, and righteousness like a stream that never runs dry.[^24]
וְיִגַּ֥ל כַּמַּ֖יִם מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה כְּנַ֥חַל אֵיתָֽן׃
Did you bring me sacrifices and grain offerings in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
הַזְּבָחִ֨ים וּמִנְחָ֜ה הִֽגַּשְׁתֶּם־לִ֧י בַמִּדְבָּ֛ר אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
You will carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your god,[^25] which you made for yourselves,
וּנְשָׂאתֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת סִכּ֣וּת מַלְכְּכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת כִּיּ֣וּן צַלְמֵיכֶ֑ם כּוֹכַב֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם לָכֶֽם׃
and I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,[^26] says the LORD, whose name is the God of Armies.
וְהִגְלֵיתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵהָ֣לְאָה לְדַמָּ֑שֶׂק אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *qinah*, a funeral song. Verse 2 is in the rhythm of such a song, with a long line followed by a short one.
n.2: Literally "the virgin of Israel", Israel pictured as a young woman who has died before her time.
n.3: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: An ancient shrine in the far south of Judah (Genesis 21:33; 26:23–25). On Bethel and Gilgal, see 4:4.
n.5: Two plays on words. *Ha-gilgal galoh yigleh*, "Gilgal will surely go into exile". *Bethel*, "house of God", will become *aven*, "nothing" or "wickedness". Hosea uses Beth-aven, "house of wickedness", as a mocking name for Bethel (Hosea 4:15).
n.6: The northern kingdom, whose chief tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh, were descended from Joseph. Also in verse 15.
n.8: Hebrew *kimah* and *kesil*, two constellations, probably the Pleiades and Orion (Job 9:9; 38:31). This is the second of the three hymns in Amos (see 4:13).
n.9: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", sometimes understood as "the shadow of death" (Psalm 23:4).
n.10: The Hebrew verb, found only here and in a few other places, is uncertain. Literally perhaps "makes destruction smile". Or "brings destruction suddenly".
n.11: The open space by the city gate, where the elders heard cases and settled disputes. Also in verses 12 and 15.
n.12: Hebrew *boshaskhem*, found only here. Perhaps "you levy taxes on the poor", which fits the next words.
n.14: Hebrew *kofer*, a payment that buys someone's release from the penalty they deserve (Numbers 35:31).
n.15: Hebrew *YHWH Elohei tseva'ot*, "the LORD, the God of Armies". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Compare "the LORD of Armies", traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". Also in verses 15, 16 and 27.
n.16: Hebrew *Adonai*, "the Lord", not the name YHWH.
n.17: Hebrew *ho ho*, a cry of grief, related to *hoy* (verse 18).
n.18: Professional mourners, often women (Jeremiah 9:16, 9:17 in most English Bibles).
n.19: As the LORD passed through Egypt on the night of the Passover (Exodus 12:12).
n.20: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning for the dead ("Alas!", 1 Kings 13:30). The prophets use it to announce disaster, and in that sense it is translated "Woe to" throughout this book.
n.21: The day when the LORD would act in power. The people expected it to bring victory and light for Israel.
n.22: Hebrew *atsarah*, a festive gathering for worship. Literally "I will not smell your solemn assemblies", the pleasing smell of their offerings (Leviticus 26:31).
n.23: Hebrew *shelem*, the sacrifice shared in a meal by the worshipers (Leviticus 3; 7:11–21).
n.24: Hebrew *nachal eitan*, "a lasting stream". Most streams in the land flow only in the rainy season.
n.25: *Sikkuth* and *Kiyyun* are probably names of Mesopotamian gods connected with the planet Saturn, known from Assyrian texts as Sakkut and Kaiwan. The Hebrew vowels make them sound like *shiqquts*, "detestable thing". Or "the shrine of your king and the stand of your images". The Septuagint reads "You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, their images", and Acts 7:42–43 quotes verses 25–27 in that form. *You will carry* may also be translated "You carried".

v: Woe to[^1] those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the first of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
ה֚וֹי הַשַּׁאֲנַנִּ֣ים בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וְהַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בְּהַ֣ר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן נְקֻבֵי֙ רֵאשִׁ֣ית הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבָ֥אוּ לָהֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Cross over to Calneh and look; go from there to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines.[^2] Are they better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
עִבְר֤וּ כַֽלְנֵה֙ וּרְא֔וּ וּלְכ֥וּ מִשָּׁ֖ם חֲמַ֣ת רַבָּ֑ה וּרְד֣וּ גַת־פְּלִשְׁתּ֗ים הֲטוֹבִים֙ מִן־הַמַּמְלָכ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה אִם־רַ֥ב גְּבוּלָ֖ם מִגְּבֻלְכֶֽם׃
You push away the day of disaster, yet you bring near the reign of violence.[^3]
הַֽמְנַדִּ֖ים לְי֣וֹם רָ֑ע וַתַּגִּישׁ֖וּן שֶׁ֥בֶת חָמָֽס׃
They lie on beds of ivory and sprawl on their couches. They eat lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
הַשֹּֽׁכְבִים֙ עַל־מִטּ֣וֹת שֵׁ֔ן וּסְרֻחִ֖ים עַל־עַרְשׂוֹתָ֑ם וְאֹכְלִ֤ים כָּרִים֙ מִצֹּ֔אן וַעֲגָלִ֖ים מִתּ֥וֹךְ מַרְבֵּֽק׃
They improvise[^4] to the sound of the harp; like David, they invent musical instruments for themselves.
הַפֹּרְטִ֖ים עַל־פִּ֣י הַנָּ֑בֶל כְּדָוִ֕יד חָשְׁב֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם כְּלֵי־שִֽׁיר׃
They drink wine by the bowlful[^5] and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but they do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
הַשֹּׁתִ֤ים בְּמִזְרְקֵי֙ יַ֔יִן וְרֵאשִׁ֥ית שְׁמָנִ֖ים יִמְשָׁ֑חוּ וְלֹ֥א נֶחְל֖וּ עַל־שֵׁ֥בֶר יוֹסֵֽף
Therefore they will now go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the feasting[^6] of those who sprawl will come to an end.
לָכֵ֛ן עַתָּ֥ה יִגְל֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ גֹּלִ֑ים וְסָ֖ר מִרְזַ֥ח סְרוּחִֽים׃ פ
The Lord GOD[^7] has sworn by himself,[^8] declares the LORD,[^9] the God of Armies:[^10] I loathe the pride of Jacob and hate his fortresses. I will hand over the city and everything in it.
נִשְׁבַּע֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ נְאֻם־יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֔וֹת מְתָאֵ֤ב אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֶת־גְּא֣וֹן יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאַרְמְנֹתָ֖יו שָׂנֵ֑אתִי וְהִסְגַּרְתִּ֖י עִ֥יר וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃
If ten men are left in one house, they will die.
וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־יִוָּ֨תְר֜וּ עֲשָׂרָ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֛ים בְּבַ֥יִת אֶחָ֖ד וָמֵֽתוּ׃

And when a relative, the one who burns the dead,[^11] picks up a body to carry the bones out of the house, he will say to someone in the back of the house, "Is anyone else with you?" He will say, "No one." Then he will say, "Hush! We must not mention the name of the LORD."[^12]

וּנְשָׂא֞וֹ דּוֹד֣וֹ וּמְסָרְפ֗וֹ לְהוֹצִ֣יא עֲצָמִים֮ מִן־הַבַּיִת֒ וְאָמַ֞ר לַאֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת הַע֥וֹד עִמָּ֖ךְ וְאָמַ֣ר אָ֑פֶס וְאָמַ֣ר הָ֔ס כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לְהַזְכִּ֖יר בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
For look, the LORD is giving the command, and he will strike the great house into fragments and the small house into splinters.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְצַוֶּ֔ה וְהִכָּ֛ה הַבַּ֥יִת הַגָּד֖וֹל רְסִיסִ֑ים וְהַבַּ֥יִת הַקָּטֹ֖ן בְּקִעִֽים׃
Do horses run on rock? Does anyone plow there with oxen?[^13] Yet you have turned justice into poison[^14] and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
הַיְרֻצ֤וּן בַּסֶּ֙לַע֙ סוּסִ֔ים אִֽם־יַחֲר֖וֹשׁ בַּבְּקָרִ֑ים כִּֽי־הֲפַכְתֶּ֤ם לְרֹאשׁ֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּפְרִ֥י צְדָקָ֖ה לְלַעֲנָֽה׃
You who rejoice over Lo-debar,[^15] who say, "Did we not take Karnaim for ourselves by our own strength?"
הַשְּׂמֵחִ֖ים לְלֹ֣א דָבָ֑ר הָאֹ֣מְרִ֔ים הֲל֣וֹא בְחָזְקֵ֔נוּ לָקַ֥חְנוּ לָ֖נוּ קַרְנָֽיִם׃
For look, I am raising up a nation against you, house of Israel, declares the LORD, the God of Armies, and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah.[^16]
כִּ֡י הִנְנִי֩ מֵקִ֨ים עֲלֵיכֶ֜ם בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נְאֻם־יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַצְּבָא֖וֹת גּ֑וֹי וְלָחֲצ֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִלְּב֥וֹא חֲמָ֖ת עַד־נַ֥חַל הָעֲרָבָֽה׃ ס

n.2: Calneh and Hamath were cities in northern Syria, and Gath one of the five Philistine cities. All three had been conquered (Isaiah 10:9; 2 Kings 12:18, 12:17 in most English Bibles). The point may be that Israel is no safer than they were.
n.3: Literally "the seat of violence", perhaps a court of injustice.
n.4: Hebrew *paratim*, found only here. Perhaps "strum" or "sing idle songs".
n.5: Literally "from bowls". The word is used for the large bowls in which the blood of sacrifices was collected (Exodus 27:3).
n.6: Hebrew *marzeach*, a feast held by a group of wealthy men, sometimes in connection with mourning (Jeremiah 16:5). *Sprawl* is the word used in verse 4.
n.7: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.9: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *Declares the LORD* is Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verse 14.
n.10: Hebrew *YHWH Elohei tseva'ot*. See 4:13. Also in verse 14.
n.11: The meaning is uncertain. Literally "his uncle and the one who burns him". Burning the dead was unusual in Israel and may point to a plague. Or "the one who burns spices for him" in honor of the dead (Jeremiah 34:5).
n.12: To call on the LORD, even in a blessing or a vow, might draw his attention and bring more death.
n.13: Literally "Does one plow with the oxen?" The same letters, divided into words differently, can be read "Does one plow the sea with oxen?"
n.14: Hebrew *rosh*, a poisonous plant. On wormwood, see 5:7.
n.15: Hebrew *lo davar*, which means "nothing". Lo-debar and Karnaim, "horns", a picture of strength, were towns in Gilead, east of the Jordan, which Israel had recently taken back from Aram (2 Samuel 9:4; 2 Kings 14:25).
n.16: Lebo-hamath, "the entrance to Hamath", was on the northern border of Israel, and the Wadi of the Arabah near the Dead Sea, in the south. These were the borders that Jeroboam II had restored (2 Kings 14:25).

v: This is what the Lord GOD[^1] showed me: he was forming a swarm of locusts[^2] when the late crop[^3] was beginning to come up. It was the late crop after the king's mowings.[^4]
כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֙נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּה֙ יוֹצֵ֣ר גֹּבַ֔י בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת עֲל֣וֹת הַלָּ֑קֶשׁ וְהִ֨נֵּה־לֶ֔קֶשׁ אַחַ֖ר גִּזֵּ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
When they had finished eating the plants of the land, I said, "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How can Jacob survive?[^5] He is so small."
וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־כִּלָּה֙ לֶֽאֱכֹל֙ אֶת־עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ סְֽלַֽח־נָ֔א מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא׃
The LORD relented[^6] concerning this. "It will not happen," said the LORD.
נִחַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־זֹ֑את לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
This is what the Lord GOD showed me: the Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire.[^7] It devoured the great deep[^8] and was devouring the land.[^9]
כֹּ֤ה הִרְאַ֙נִי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה קֹרֵ֛א לָרִ֥ב בָּאֵ֖שׁ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וַתֹּ֙אכַל֙ אֶת־תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וְאָכְלָ֖ה אֶת־הַחֵֽלֶק׃
Then I said, "Lord GOD, stop, please! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."
וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ חֲדַל־נָ֔א מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא׃
The LORD relented concerning this. "This too will not happen," said the Lord GOD.
נִחַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־זֹ֑את גַּם־הִיא֙ לֹ֣א תִֽהְיֶ֔ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ ס
This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing beside a wall built with a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.[^10]
כֹּ֣ה הִרְאַ֔נִי וְהִנֵּ֧ה אֲדֹנָ֛י נִצָּ֖ב עַל־חוֹמַ֣ת אֲנָ֑ךְ וּבְיָד֖וֹ אֲנָֽךְ׃
The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am setting a plumb line among my people Israel. I will not pass them by again.[^11]
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י מָֽה־אַתָּ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ עָמ֔וֹס וָאֹמַ֖ר אֲנָ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י הִנְנִ֨י שָׂ֤ם אֲנָךְ֙ בְּקֶ֙רֶב֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־אוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד עֲב֥וֹר לֽוֹ׃
The high places[^12] of Isaac[^13] will be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste. I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
וְנָשַׁ֙מּוּ֙ בָּמ֣וֹת יִשְׂחָ֔ק וּמִקְדְּשֵׁ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יֶחֱרָ֑בוּ וְקַמְתִּ֛י עַל־בֵּ֥ית יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ פ
Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent a message to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos has conspired against you in the very heart of the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words.
וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל אֶל־יָרָבְעָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר קָשַׁ֨ר עָלֶ֜יךָ עָמ֗וֹס בְּקֶ֙רֶב֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹא־תוּכַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ לְהָכִ֖יל אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרָֽיו׃
For this is what Amos has said: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
כִּי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר עָמ֔וֹס בַּחֶ֖רֶב יָמ֣וּת יָרָבְעָ֑ם וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל גָּלֹ֥ה יִגְלֶ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃ ס
Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer,[^14] go! Run away to the land of Judah. Earn your living[^15] there, and prophesy there.
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲמַצְיָה֙ אֶל־עָמ֔וֹס חֹזֶ֕ה לֵ֥ךְ בְּרַח־לְךָ֖ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה וֶאֱכָל־שָׁ֣ם לֶ֔חֶם וְשָׁ֖ם תִּנָּבֵֽא׃
But never prophesy at Bethel again, for it is the king's sanctuary and a royal temple."[^16]
וּבֵֽית־אֵ֔ל לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד לְהִנָּבֵ֑א כִּ֤י מִקְדַּשׁ־מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ ה֔וּא וּבֵ֥ית מַמְלָכָ֖ה הֽוּא׃ ס
Amos answered Amaziah, "I am not a prophet, and I am not a prophet's son.[^17] I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.[^18]
וַיַּ֤עַן עָמוֹס֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־אֲמַצְיָ֔ה לֹא־נָבִ֣יא אָנֹ֔כִי וְלֹ֥א בֶן־נָבִ֖יא אָנֹ֑כִי כִּֽי־בוֹקֵ֥ר אָנֹ֖כִי וּבוֹלֵ֥ס שִׁקְמִֽים׃
But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'
וַיִּקָּחֵ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י הַצֹּ֑אן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ יְהוָ֔ה לֵ֥ךְ הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
So now hear the word of the LORD. You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach[^19] against the house of Isaac.'
וְעַתָּ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֗ר לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תַטִּ֖יף עַל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂחָֽק׃

Therefore this is what the LORD says: Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be divided up with a measuring line, and you yourself will die in an unclean land.[^20] And Israel will surely go into exile away from its land."

לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֞ בָּעִ֤יר תִּזְנֶה֙ וּבָנֶ֤יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וְאַדְמָתְךָ֖ בַּחֶ֣בֶל תְּחֻלָּ֑ק וְאַתָּ֗ה עַל־אֲדָמָ֤ה טְמֵאָה֙ תָּמ֔וּת וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל גָּלֹ֥ה יִגְלֶ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Also in verses 2, 4, 5 and 6.
n.2: Hebrew *govai*, a word for locusts not among the four in Joel 1:4 (compare Nahum 3:17).
n.3: Hebrew *leqesh*, the later growth of grass and grain after the spring rains.
n.4: Perhaps the first cutting of the grass, taken as a tax for the king's animals (1 Kings 18:5). After it, the late crop was all the people had.
n.5: Literally "Who is Jacob, that he could stand?" Also in verse 5.
n.6: Or "changed his mind". Also in verse 6.
n.7: Literally "calling to contend by fire", as in a lawsuit. Some scholars read "calling for a shower of fire", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.8: Hebrew *tehom rabbah*, the waters under the earth that fed the springs and rivers (Genesis 7:11).
n.9: Literally "the portion", perhaps the land allotted to Israel.
n.10: Hebrew *anakh*, found only in verses 7–8. The traditional meaning is "plumb line", a cord with a weight of lead, used to test whether a wall stands straight. The word may instead mean "tin", a metal used in making weapons: "standing on a wall of tin, with tin in his hand".
n.11: That is, I will no longer pass over their sins and spare them. Also in 8:2.
n.12: Hill shrines where sacrifices were offered.
n.13: A poetic name for Israel, found only in Amos (also verse 16). Isaac was the father of Jacob.
n.14: Hebrew *chozeh*, "one who sees visions", from the verb in 1:1.
n.17: The Hebrew has no verb. Or "I was not a prophet …; I was a herdsman". A *prophet's son* is a member of a group of prophets (2 Kings 2:3, 5).
n.18: The fruit of the sycamore-fig tree had to be slit or pinched to make it ripen. The tree does not grow at the height of Tekoa (1:1), so Amos may have worked in the lowlands.
n.19: Literally "drip", as words flow from the mouth (Micah 2:6, 11).
n.20: A foreign land, unclean because other gods are worshiped there.

v: This is what the Lord GOD[^1] showed me: a basket of summer fruit.[^2]
כֹּ֥ה הִרְאַ֖נִי אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה כְּל֥וּב קָֽיִץ׃
He said, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end[^3] has come for my people Israel. I will not pass them by again.[^4]
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מָֽה־אַתָּ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ עָמ֔וֹס וָאֹמַ֖ר כְּל֣וּב קָ֑יִץ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י בָּ֤א הַקֵּץ֙ אֶל־עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹא־אוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד עֲב֥וֹר לֽוֹ׃
On that day the songs of the temple[^5] will become wailing, declares the Lord GOD.[^6] So many corpses, thrown out everywhere! Hush!"[^7]
וְהֵילִ֜ילוּ שִׁיר֤וֹת הֵיכָל֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה רַ֣ב הַפֶּ֔גֶר בְּכָל־מָק֖וֹם הִשְׁלִ֥יךְ הָֽס׃ פ
Hear this, you who trample[^8] the needy and bring the poor of the land[^9] to an end,
שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֕את הַשֹּׁאֲפִ֖ים אֶבְי֑וֹן וְלַשְׁבִּ֖ית *ענוי־**עֲנִיֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃

who say, "When will the new moon be over, so that we can sell grain, and the Sabbath, so that we can open the stores of wheat?[^10] We will make the ephah small and the shekel heavy[^11] and cheat with dishonest scales,
לֵאמֹ֗ר מָתַ֞י יַעֲבֹ֤ר הַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ וְנַשְׁבִּ֣ירָה שֶּׁ֔בֶר וְהַשַּׁבָּ֖ת וְנִפְתְּחָה־בָּ֑ר לְהַקְטִ֤ין אֵיפָה֙ וּלְהַגְדִּ֣יל שֶׁ֔קֶל וּלְעַוֵּ֖ת מֹאזְנֵ֥י מִרְמָֽה׃
buying the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals,[^12] and selling even the sweepings of the wheat."
לִקְנ֤וֹת בַּכֶּ֙סֶף֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְאֶבְי֖וֹן בַּעֲב֣וּר נַעֲלָ֑יִם וּמַפַּ֥ל בַּ֖ר נַשְׁבִּֽיר׃
The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob:[^13] I will never forget anything they have done.
נִשְׁבַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה בִּגְא֣וֹן יַעֲקֹ֑ב אִם־אֶשְׁכַּ֥ח לָנֶ֖צַח כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃
Will not the land tremble because of this, and everyone who lives in it mourn? All of it will rise like the Nile,[^14] be tossed about, and sink again like the river of Egypt.
הַ֤עַל זֹאת֙ לֹֽא־תִרְגַּ֣ז הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאָבַ֖ל כָּל־יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בָּ֑הּ וְעָלְתָ֤ה כָאֹר֙ כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְנִגְרְשָׁ֥ה *ונשקה **וְנִשְׁקְעָ֖ה כִּיא֥וֹר מִצְרָֽיִם׃ ס
On that day, declares the Lord GOD, I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.[^15]
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם וְהַחֲשַׁכְתִּ֥י לָאָ֖רֶץ בְּי֥וֹם אֽוֹר׃

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into a lament. I will put sackcloth on every waist and shave every head bald.[^16] I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
וְהָפַכְתִּ֨י חַגֵּיכֶ֜ם לְאֵ֗בֶל וְכָל־שִֽׁירֵיכֶם֙ לְקִינָ֔ה וְהַעֲלֵיתִ֤י עַל־כָּל־מָתְנַ֙יִם֙ שָׂ֔ק וְעַל־כָּל־רֹ֖אשׁ קָרְחָ֑ה וְשַׂמְתִּ֙יהָ֙ כְּאֵ֣בֶל יָחִ֔יד וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ כְּי֥וֹם מָֽר׃
Look, the days are coming, declares the Lord GOD, when I will send a famine on the land: not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.
הִנֵּ֣ה ׀ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֗ים נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְהִשְׁלַחְתִּ֥י רָעָ֖ב בָּאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא־רָעָ֤ב לַלֶּ֙חֶם֙ וְלֹֽא־צָמָ֣א לַמַּ֔יִם כִּ֣י אִם־לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
People will stagger from sea to sea[^17] and wander from north to east, running back and forth to seek the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
וְנָעוּ֙ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־יָ֔ם וּמִצָּפ֖וֹן וְעַד־מִזְרָ֑ח יְשֽׁ[m]וֹטְט֛וּ לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־דְּבַר־יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יִמְצָֽאוּ׃
On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst.
בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא תִּ֠תְעַלַּפְנָה הַבְּתוּלֹ֧ת הַיָּפ֛וֹת וְהַבַּחוּרִ֖ים בַּצָּמָֽא׃
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria,[^18] who say, "As your god lives, Dan," and "As the way to Beersheba lives,"[^19] will fall and never rise again.
הַנִּשְׁבָּעִים֙ בְּאַשְׁמַ֣ת שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וְאָמְר֗וּ חֵ֤י אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ דָּ֔ן וְחֵ֖י דֶּ֣רֶךְ בְּאֵֽר־שָׁ֑בַע וְנָפְל֖וּ וְלֹא־יָק֥וּמוּ עֽוֹד׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The Lord GOD* is also in verses 3, 9 and 11.
n.2: Hebrew *kelub qayits*. *Qayits* is the fruit of late summer, chiefly figs, gathered at the end of the farming year.
n.3: Hebrew *qets*, "end". The vision rests on a play on words: *qayits*, "summer fruit", sounds like *qets*, "end". The ripe fruit at the end of the year points to Israel's end.
n.5: Or "palace". Some scholars read "the singing women of the palace", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.6: Hebrew *ne'um Adonai YHWH*, "the declaration of the Lord GOD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 9 and 11.
n.7: The Hebrew is abrupt. Literally "Many the corpse; in every place he has thrown; hush!" Compare 6:10.
n.9: The Hebrew text is written "the humble of the land" but read "the poor of the land".
n.10: Trading stopped on the new moon and the Sabbath (2 Kings 4:23; Nehemiah 10:32, 10:31 in most English Bibles). *Open the stores of wheat*: literally "open wheat".
n.11: The ephah was the measure in which grain was sold, probably about 22 liters (two-thirds of a bushel). The shekel was the weight, about 2/5 ounce (11.5 grams), used to weigh the buyer's silver. A small measure and a heavy weight cheated the buyer twice.
n.13: Perhaps a title of God, like "the Glory of Israel" (1 Samuel 15:29). Or the LORD swears by the arrogance of Jacob (6:8), which is as sure not to change as his own oath.
n.14: Hebrew *ka'or*, "like the light", probably a short spelling of *kay'or*, "like the Nile", as in 9:5. The Nile rose in flood every year and fell again.
n.15: Perhaps an eclipse of the sun. One took place on 15 June 763 BC and was recorded in Assyria.
n.16: Literally "I will bring up sackcloth on all waists and baldness on every head". Wearing sackcloth and shaving the head were signs of mourning (Isaiah 15:2–3; Micah 1:16).
n.17: From the Dead Sea in the east to the Mediterranean in the west, that is, the length and breadth of the land.
n.18: Perhaps a mocking name for a goddess worshiped in Samaria, Ashima (2 Kings 17:30), or for the calf of Bethel (Hosea 8:5–6).
n.19: Dan, in the far north, and Beersheba, in the far south, had shrines (1 Kings 12:29; Amos 5:5). *The way to Beersheba* may be the pilgrimage to its shrine. Some scholars read "As your god lives, Beersheba", with a small change to the Hebrew.

v: I saw the Lord[^1] standing beside the altar,[^2] and he said: Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake, and shatter them on the heads of all the people.[^3] Those who are left of them I will kill with the sword. Not one of them will get away; not one will escape.

רָאִ֨יתִי אֶת־אֲדֹנָ֜י נִצָּ֣ב עַֽל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הַ֨ךְ הַכַּפְתּ֜וֹר וְיִרְעֲשׁ֣וּ הַסִּפִּ֗ים וּבְצַ֙עַם֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ כֻּלָּ֔ם וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖ם בַּחֶ֣רֶב אֶהֱרֹ֑ג לֹֽא־יָנ֤וּס לָהֶם֙ נָ֔ס וְלֹֽא־יִמָּלֵ֥ט לָהֶ֖ם פָּלִֽיט׃
If they dig down into Sheol,[^4] from there my hand will take them. If they climb up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.
אִם־יַחְתְּר֣וּ בִשְׁא֔וֹל מִשָּׁ֖ם יָדִ֣י תִקָּחֵ֑ם וְאִֽם־יַעֲלוּ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם מִשָּׁ֖ם אוֹרִידֵֽם׃

If they hide on the top of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them. If they hide from my sight on the floor of the sea, from there I will command the serpent,[^5] and it will bite them.
וְאִם־יֵחָֽבְאוּ֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל מִשָּׁ֥ם אֲחַפֵּ֖שׂ וּלְקַחְתִּ֑ים וְאִם־יִסָּ֨תְר֜וּ מִנֶּ֤גֶד עֵינַי֙ בְּקַרְקַ֣ע הַיָּ֔ם מִשָּׁ֛ם אֲצַוֶּ֥ה אֶת־הַנָּחָ֖שׁ וּנְשָׁכָֽם׃
If they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes on them for harm and not for good.
וְאִם־יֵלְכ֤וּ בַשְּׁבִי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹֽיבֵיהֶ֔ם מִשָּׁ֛ם אֲצַוֶּ֥ה אֶת־הַחֶ֖רֶב וַהֲרָגָ֑תַם וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י עֵינִ֧י עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם לְרָעָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א לְטוֹבָֽה׃
The Lord GOD of Armies[^6] touches the earth, and it melts, and all who live in it mourn. All of it rises like the Nile and sinks again like the river of Egypt.
וַאדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה הַצְּבָא֗וֹת הַנּוֹגֵ֤עַ בָּאָ֙רֶץ֙ וַתָּמ֔וֹג וְאָבְל֖וּ כָּל־י֣וֹשְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ וְעָלְתָ֤ה כַיְאֹר֙ כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְשָׁקְעָ֖ה כִּיאֹ֥ר מִצְרָֽיִם

He builds his upper rooms[^7] in the heavens and sets the foundations of his vault[^8] on the earth. He calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth: the LORD is his name.
הַבּוֹנֶ֤ה בַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ *מעלותו **מַעֲלוֹתָ֔יו וַאֲגֻדָּת֖וֹ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ יְסָדָ֑הּ הַקֹּרֵ֣א לְמֵֽי־הַיָּ֗ם וַֽיִּשְׁפְּכֵ֛ם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃
Are you not like the Cushites[^9] to me, people of Israel? declares the LORD.[^10] Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor,[^11] and the Arameans from Kir?
הֲל֣וֹא כִבְנֵי֩ כֻשִׁיִּ֨ים אַתֶּ֥ם לִ֛י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה הֲל֣וֹא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הֶעֱלֵ֙יתִי֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּפְלִשְׁתִּיִּ֥ים מִכַּפְתּ֖וֹר וַאֲרָ֥ם מִקִּֽיר׃
Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not completely destroy the house of Jacob, declares the LORD.
הִנֵּ֞ה עֵינֵ֣י ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה בַּמַּמְלָכָה֙ הַֽחַטָּאָ֔ה וְהִשְׁמַדְתִּ֣י אֹתָ֔הּ מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֑ה אֶ֗פֶס כִּ֠י לֹ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֥יד אַשְׁמִ֛יד אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יַעֲקֹ֖ב נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
For look, I am giving the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble[^12] falls to the ground.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ מְצַוֶּ֔ה וַהֲנִע֥וֹתִי בְכָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִנּ֙וֹעַ֙ בַּכְּבָרָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יִפּ֥וֹל צְר֖וֹר אָֽרֶץ׃
All the sinners among my people will die by the sword, those who say, "Disaster will not come near us or overtake us."
בַּחֶ֣רֶב יָמ֔וּתוּ כֹּ֖ל חַטָּאֵ֣י עַמִּ֑י הָאֹמְרִ֗ים לֹֽא־תַגִּ֧ישׁ וְתַקְדִּ֛ים בַּעֲדֵ֖ינוּ הָרָעָֽה׃
On that day I will raise up the fallen shelter[^13] of David. I will repair its broken walls and raise up its ruins, and I will rebuild it as it was in days of old,
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אָקִ֛ים אֶת־סֻכַּ֥ת דָּוִ֖יד הַנֹּפֶ֑לֶת וְגָדַרְתִּ֣י אֶת־פִּרְצֵיהֶ֗ן וַהֲרִֽסֹתָיו֙ אָקִ֔ים וּבְנִיתִ֖יהָ כִּימֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
so that they may take possession of what is left of Edom and of all the nations that are called by my name,[^14] declares the LORD, who will do this.[^15]
לְמַ֨עַן יִֽירְשׁ֜וּ אֶת־שְׁאֵרִ֤ית אֱדוֹם֙ וְכָל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שְׁמִ֖י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה עֹ֥שֶׂה זֹּֽאת׃ פ

Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when the one who plows will overtake the one who reaps, and the one who treads grapes the one who sows the seed.[^16] The mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.[^17]
הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְנִגַּ֤שׁ חוֹרֵשׁ֙ בַּקֹּצֵ֔ר וְדֹרֵ֥ךְ עֲנָבִ֖ים בְּמֹשֵׁ֣ךְ הַזָּ֑רַע וְהִטִּ֤יפוּ הֶֽהָרִים֙ עָסִ֔יס וְכָל־הַגְּבָע֖וֹת תִּתְמוֹגַֽגְנָה׃
I will restore the fortunes[^18] of my people Israel. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them; they will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
וְשַׁבְתִּי֮ אֶת־שְׁב֣וּת עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וּבָנ֞וּ עָרִ֤ים נְשַׁמּוֹת֙ וְיָשָׁ֔בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְשָׁת֖וּ אֶת־יֵינָ֑ם וְעָשׂ֣וּ גַנּ֔וֹת וְאָכְל֖וּ אֶת־פְּרִיהֶֽם׃
I will plant them on their land, and they will never again be uprooted from the land that I have given them, says the LORD your God.
וּנְטַעְתִּ֖ים עַל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וְלֹ֨א יִנָּתְשׁ֜וּ ע֗וֹד מֵעַ֤ל אַדְמָתָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

n.1: Hebrew *Adonai*, "the Lord", not the name YHWH.
n.3: Literally "shatter them on the head of all of them". The meaning is uncertain.
n.4: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. Compare Psalm 139:7–10.
n.5: The monster of the sea, as in Isaiah 27:1.
n.6: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH ha-tseva'ot*, "the Lord GOD of the Armies". *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Verses 5–6 are the third of the three hymns in Amos (see 4:13).
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "his upper room" but read "his upper rooms". Or "his stairs".
n.8: Hebrew *aguddah*, "a band, a bundle", here probably the dome of the sky, pictured as resting on the earth.
n.9: The people of Cush, the land south of Egypt on the upper Nile, at the far edge of the world Israel knew.
n.10: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 8, 12 and 13.
n.11: Probably Crete, from where the Philistines had come (Deuteronomy 2:23; Jeremiah 47:4). On Kir, see 1:5.
n.12: Hebrew *tseror*, "pebble", or perhaps "kernel". A sieve lets the grain fall through and keeps back the stones: no sinner will escape. If the word means "kernel", the point is that not one grain will be lost.
n.13: Hebrew *sukkah*, a hut or booth. The royal house of David is pictured as a shelter that has fallen down. *Its broken walls* is literally "their breaches", perhaps of the two kingdoms, Israel and Judah.
n.14: Literally "over whom my name is called", that is, which belong to me.
n.15: Acts 15:16–17 quotes verses 11–12 from the Greek Septuagint, which reads in verse 12 "so that the rest of humankind, and all the nations over whom my name is called, may seek", where Acts adds "the Lord". The Septuagint follows a Hebrew text that read *adam*, "humankind", for *edom*, "Edom", and *yidreshu*, "they will seek", for *yirshu*, "they will take possession". The quotation in Acts also begins "After this I will return".
n.16: The harvest will be so large that it lasts until the time comes to plow and sow again (Leviticus 26:5).
n.17: Literally "will melt". Compare Joel 4:18 (3:18 in most English Bibles).
n.18: Literally "turn the turning", an idiom for restoring what was lost. Or "bring back the captives".
